search_root_note: Ground truth was verified only against src/itsdangerous/ (the library itself). tests/test_itsdangerous/ also calls several of these functions (e.g. want_bytes, unsign) but resolving those call sites requires tracing pytest fixture indirection (which concrete Signer subclass a given fixture constructs) that is beyond what static text search, ctags, or corbel's static analysis can be expected to determine, and beyond what was feasible to hand-verify exhaustively here. All four tools are scoped to src/ uniformly - including corbel, whose own repo-wide index results are filtered to src/ before scoring - so no tool is advantaged or penalized by the test suite's presence.
verification_method: Direct reading of source files via the Read tool, with ripgrep used to enumerate candidate line numbers and a small standalone Python script (not corbel) used to map each matched line to its nearest preceding `def` at or before that line, whose output was then spot-checked against the actual source for every entry below. corbel was never executed to produce any answer in this file.

entries.verification_note: want_bytes is a unique, unambiguous name across the package with 19 real call sites (18 outside its own file plus 2 inside encoding.py itself, at lines 24 and 32, inside sibling functions base64_encode/base64_decode). Every line above was individually opened and read; several sit inside classes with multiple same-name overload stubs (Signer.__init__ has 6 @overload-decorated signatures at lines 108-190, TimestampSigner.unsign has 2 @t.overload stubs at 57/65 before the real implementation at 72) so the enclosing-def search intentionally walks to the nearest preceding `def` regardless of decorator, which lands on the real (non-stub) implementation in every case here since typing stubs have no body to call anything from.

`get_signature` is defined 4 times in this package: SigningAlgorithm.get_signature (abstract, signer.py:20, 2 args beyond self), NoneAlgorithm.get_signature (signer.py:36, 2 args), HMACAlgorithm.get_signature (signer.py:62, 2 args), and Signer.get_signature (this entry, signer.py:215, 1 arg beyond self). This entry targets specifically Signer.get_signature. `rg -n "get_signature\(" src/` returns 7 lines total: the declaration/2 other definitions (20,36,62), one call inside get_signature itself to a *different* get_signature (signer.py:219, self.algorithm.get_signature(key, value) - 2-arg form, targets the SigningAlgorithm family, not this entry - see itsdangerous-03), and the 2 real 1-arg callers of this entry listed above. A tool that cannot distinguish the 1-arg Signer.get_signature call shape from the 2-arg SigningAlgorithm.get_signature call shape will over-count.

ground_truth.name: get_signature
ground_truth.note: self.algorithm.get_signature(key, value) at signer.py:219; self.algorithm: SigningAlgorithm is duck-typed and set to a NoneAlgorithm (signer.py:36) or HMACAlgorithm (signer.py:62) instance at construction time (Signer.__init__ digest_method parameter), not determinable from this call site alone.

entries.verification_note: Python has no static trait-object type the way Rust does, but the effect is identical: self.algorithm is typed SigningAlgorithm (an unenforced duck-typed base with only an interface contract, signer.py:15-24) and get_signature's actual target is chosen by whichever concrete class was assigned to self.algorithm at runtime. No single verified_callees entry is correct in isolation; NoneAlgorithm.get_signature and HMACAlgorithm.get_signature are equally valid targets from source alone. This is the Python duck-typing counterpart to hyperfine-06 and corbel-05's Rust dyn-trait dispatch.

`unsign` is also defined on TimestampSigner (timed.py, 2 @t.overload stubs at 57/65 plus the real implementation at 72), which overrides this Signer.unsign for timed serializers. The 3 callers listed all statically resolve to this base Signer.unsign: timed.py:89 uses explicit `super()`, which Python resolves via TimestampSigner's single base class (Signer) with no ambiguity; signer.py:263 is a same-class call; serializer.py:339 calls `.unsign(...)` on a variable whose declared/constructed type in Serializer.loads's own code path is plain Signer (TimedSerializer overrides loads/loads_unsafe separately in timed.py rather than reusing this path). rg -n "\.unsign\(" src/ returns exactly these 3 non-definition lines plus one more, timed.py:164, which calls self.unsign on a TimestampSigner instance (excluded from this entry's ground truth since it targets TimestampSigner.unsign, not Signer.unsign).

ground_truth.name: __init__
ground_truth.note: Serializer.make_signer (serializer.py:278-285) constructs the active signer as `self.signer(self.secret_keys, salt=salt, **self.signer_kwargs)` at serializer.py:285, where `self.signer: type[Signer]` is a class attribute set from the `signer` constructor parameter (default `Signer`, serializer.py:99 `default_signer: type[Signer] = Signer`; overridable per-Serializer-instance). The call `self.signer(...)` is a constructor call on a type held in a variable, not a textual `Signer(` or `.__init__(` anywhere in the source - no name-based or AST call-site search targeting the literal identifier `__init__` or `Signer` will find serializer.py:285 as a call to this symbol. Within this repository specifically, the only two classes ever assigned to `self.signer` are `Signer` itself and `TimestampSigner` (timed.py:22), and TimestampSigner defines no `__init__` of its own, so in practice both possible runtime classes execute this exact Signer.__init__ - but that is an accident of this codebase's current class hierarchy, not something provable from the call site at serializer.py:285 alone (a third-party subclass with its own __init__ passed via the public `signer=` constructor argument would silently redirect it).

verification.verification_note: ADVERSARIAL. `rg -n "Signer\(" src/` and `rg -n "__init__\(" src/` both return zero real construction call sites for this class anywhere in itsdangerous's own source - Signer is never instantiated by its literal class name in-tree. The only place a Signer (or Signer subclass) is actually constructed is serializer.py:285's `self.signer(self.secret_keys, salt=salt, **self.signer_kwargs)`, where `self.signer` is a `type[Signer]` class attribute assigned from a constructor parameter (serializer.py:99,225). This is genuine config-driven dynamic dispatch on which was flagged during hand-verification (not by the mechanical scanner, whose adversarial_flags only fired 'dunder_name' on this candidate) and is the itsdangerous counterpart to corbel-05's Rust dyn-trait dispatch and itsdangerous-03's self.algorithm duck typing: the callee is real, its target set is knowable, but the call site never mentions the callee's name.
